item.title: A Child’s-Eye Memoir of the Hippie Trail: Caleb Dardick in Conversation with Rachel Howard — Sun Sep 27, 2:00 PM — Mary L. Stephens – Davis Branch Library
item.description: Join author Caleb Dardick for a vivid reading and conversation celebrating his forthcoming memoir, The Adventures of Superfreak: My Childhood on the Hippie Trail (Running Wild Press, September 21, 2026). Caleb will be in conversation with Davis author Rachel Howard, author of The Risk of Us and The Lost Night, for an evening about memory, family, counterculture, disability, and the making of a memoir. The Adventures of Superfreak offers a child’s-eye view of the counterculture—not as nostalgia, but as lived family reality, with all its longing, idealism, danger, and contradiction. In 1970, Caleb’s family set out from Amsterdam to India in a VW bus: three young children traveling with disabled parents—his father using a wheelchair, his mother living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder—on a 20,000-mile journey through Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and India. item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Sun Sep 27, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up

item.title: Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz — Tue Sep 29, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays, 10 AM – 12 PM | September 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 $170 Members, $190 Non-Members (Materials not included) This 5-week workshop with Misuk Goltz will focus on using your brushes to their full potential and practicing diverse hand motions to achieve painterly, expressive watercolor paintings. Students will learn how to distribute different values to create balanced and sophisticated artwork while painting various subjects. Please note that this class is intended for participants who have previous experience with watercolor techniques and color blending. The use of high-quality watercolor materials is strongly recommended to achieve the best results. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? item.title: Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington — Tue Sep 29, 12:00 PM — UC Davis Design Museum
item.description:
The UC Davis Design Museum opens its 2026-2027 season with Connecting Threads (together): Textile Works by Lynn Setterington which opens on Sept. 29 and runs through Nov. 20. Collaboration is at the heart of textile making and this idea is explored in a display of work by UK based artist Setterington. Through textiles the artist challenges contemporary issues in society and how stitch can be used to commemorate people and communities. She has worked with underserved communities across the globe, including the UK, India, Bangladesh, Brazil and USA. She draws on popular culture and textile history to raise awareness of societal issues. Themes range from sustainability, place, well-being and identity and belonging. This exhibition is co-sponsored by the Maria Manetti Shrem Institute for Sustainable Design, Fashion & Textiles.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: War & Disability: Interdisciplinary Perspectives on Iran and Ukraine — Tue Sep 29, 4:30 PM — International House Davis
item.description:
​As the wars in Ukraine and Iran continue to unfold, what can we learn from the experience and perspective of those with disability who are navigating the conflicts? ​The Davis Humanities Institute (DHI) is pleased to bring together leading scholars of war and disability, Professors Sarah Phillips and Sona Kazemi, for a public conversation on two of the world’s most significant, ongoing conflict zones. ​This conversation continues the DHI’s event series spotlighting interdisciplinary research on disability. The discussion will be moderated by the DHI’s Faculty Director, Professor Jenny Kaminer, and will be followed by a complimentary reception. ​Everyone welcome. Registration required (https://luma.com/imtkporv). Doors open at 4:30pm. The event will start promptly at 4:45pm.
Source: The Dirt

Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. item.title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis) — Sun Oct 25, 1:00 PM — Blanchard Room
item.description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States.
The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.
The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.
Source: Yolo Library

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Dec 24, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Shields Library Mural Dedication — Fri Oct 2, 1:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
join us in celebrating our new library mural, created by undergraduate students in the Mural Workshop (ART 171/CHI 171) in Spring 2026. Drawing on the Chicanx tradition of muralism, the students' creative process centered on community engagement, collective storytelling, and sense of place. Vibrant imagery of students, photos from the library's University Archives, and an oak tree bearing the words “Saber es Poder” (“Knowledge is Power”) are among the elements that explore the library as a space where preservation and empowerment meet. Learn more about the mural.
Meet some of the artists who created the mural and see footage of the making of this beautiful work of art. Light refreshments available while they last. Free and open to all.
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Oct 14, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants
